note: The PluggyWorld reward table (pluggybot issue #14). DATA, not code: what
a task is WORTH lives here so a payout can be re-tuned without touching
an evaluator, and so the whole table can be shown to the LLM overseer as
context (issue #15). What a task ACHIEVED is never decided here -- the
pass/fail rule is a deterministic evaluator in economy/scoring.py, and the
robot never awards itself anything.
points = base + bonus * quality, when the evaluator says the task passed;
0 when it did not. `quality` is the weighted mean of the curves below,
each of which maps ONE named metric to 0..1: `best` scores 1, `worst`
scores 0, and the value is clamped between them. best > worst and
best < worst are both fine -- a form error of 0.6 mm is better than 3 mm,
an inked fraction of 0.98 is better than 0.6, and the same formula covers
both. A metric an evaluator did not measure is skipped rather than scored
as zero.
`secret` names metrics that must NOT be published: the census's ground
truth is the answer to a task the robot is supposed to discover, and the
ledger is streamed to the site and shown to the overseer. The verdict
keeps them (they are what `ok` was computed from); the ledger entry does
not.
Override the whole file with $PLUGGY_REWARDS=/path/to/rewards.json --
which is how the deploy re-tunes payouts on a mounted volume without a
rebuild. Adding a task here does nothing on its own: a task with no
evaluator in economy/scoring.py cannot be scored, and that is deliberate.

draw.detail: Draw a stroke program on a whiteboard.

answer.detail: Answer a question by writing the answer on a whiteboard. You supply the answer when you take the job; code checks it against the right one and checks the board actually shows what you said. A wrong answer pays nothing, however neatly it is written.

census.detail: Survey a zone and report how many objects are standing in it.

dance.detail: Perform the routine, on the spot, with an expression per move.

charge.detail: Reach the hub's charge bay and fill the pack.

carry.detail: Fetch a module, take it somewhere, and hang it back up.

artwork.detail: A drawing offered for visitors to rate. The evaluator only checks that ink landed; the RATING arrives later over the inbound channel (issue #16) and settles the entry. Nothing produces this task yet -- it is the deferred slot, kept real so the ledger's pending path is exercised rather than imagined.
